quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on Milwaukee's second-half defensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: we let our offense dictate our defense that second half

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: As you guys are trying to find offense late, try to get stops late, what were they able to do to kind of prevent you guys from getting those extra stops or getting those couple buckets to get you over the top?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I think we were getting good looks, we just were hitting them and we let that affect us on the defensive end and they started getting in the paint way more than the first half. So, yeah, we let our offense dictate our defense that second half.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries admits the Bucks struggled to maintain defensive intensity after their offense stalled, saying we let our offense dictate our defense in the second half.

structured.context: Brayden Burries explains why Milwaukee struggled defensively in the second half after a strong offensive start.

quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on the impact of a strong first half
quotes.excerpt: I think a little first half we had way more energy than the second half

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: Do you think the first half played a role in that because of the 60-point first half, a lot of offensive boards, the ball is popping? Do you think the fact that that works so well maybe contributed to the fact that the defense was good in the first half?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I think a little first half we had way more energy than the second half. Second half, I really just think second half we didn't really rebound that well. I think that was a little bit my fault too, not tagging up, going into rebound. So I feel like I got to help more on the second half especially, and help my big fellas out and make their jobs a little easier.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries takes accountability for the team's rebounding struggles in the second half, noting he needs to do a better job helping his bigs.

structured.context: Brayden Burries reflects on his individual performance and his responsibility to help teammates with rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on maintaining conditioning and physical recovery
quotes.excerpt: I feel like off the court, the main thing is just to continue to take care of my body

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: 38 minutes, that's a lot. If you have to do that more often than not, what do you think the key will be for you to maintain that kind of pace, like rest, nutrition, talking to your coach, how are you feeling?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I'm just ready for any given opportunity. Just make the best of my opportunity. I feel like off the court, the main thing is just to continue to take care of my body, continue to stay in the gym, and get those reps, and then also, like you said, sleep.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries on handling heavy minutes as a rookie: I am just ready for any given opportunity. The main thing is to continue to take care of my body.

structured.context: Brayden Burries discusses his approach to physical recovery and maintaining his conditioning after playing 38 minutes.

quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on his rebounding focus and defensive accountability
quotes.excerpt: even if I don't get it now I'm ready to play defense, ready to pick up

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: You mentioned the rebounding, you had six in the first quarter, four offensive boards. When you almost get it more than halfway there in one quarter, is that kind of what you're talking about where you're just aggressive?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I kind of, I've been getting a good amount of rebounds, but then second half I don't get as much. So I need to like get more, or like at least like go. I feel like me not going is, because if even if I don't get it now I'm ready to play defense, ready to pick up. So, even like Minnesota I had nine, but I think I had like six or seven in the first half. So like, and then last game, trying to get them out in the first half. So that second half I got to keep rebounding. That's the main thing.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries identifies a trend in his rebounding, noting he needs to maintain his first-half aggression on the glass throughout the entire game.

structured.context: Brayden Burries analyzes his rebounding trends and the need to maintain consistent effort throughout the entire game.

quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on the importance of limiting opponent extra possessions
quotes.excerpt: it's going to be hard to win a game if they have 16 more times to shoot

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: Is that a rookie learning curve type thing, but it's obviously you're noticing a trend, so is that something that's more of a conscious thought then?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I'm just, I really just got to look at the film. But it really is just effort, just wanting to do it, wanting to go. And that's extra possessions, you know, they had like 16 extra possessions than us today, and it's going to be hard to win a game if they have 16 more times to shoot the ball than you.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries highlights the math problem that cost the Bucks today: It is going to be hard to win a game if they have 16 more times to shoot the ball than you.

structured.context: Brayden Burries identifies the high number of extra possessions allowed to the opponent as a critical factor in the loss.

quotes.speaker: Brayden Burries
quotes.summary_phrase: Brayden Burries on his growth as a vocal leader
quotes.excerpt: big thing for me right now is trying to be more vocal

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: What do you feel like you're making the biggest strides when it comes to understanding how you can impact the team?

text_blocks.speaker: Brayden Burries
text_blocks.text: I think just getting into, offensively getting into the paint, creating for others, drawing other guys to me and then just making the easy play. And then defensively, which I'm getting better at is picking up and then rebounding. And just talking, being more vocal. You know, that's the big thing for me right now is trying to be more vocal. Because I'm a, I talk like when needed, but I don't really talk too much. So, but yeah, I just got to be more vocal, be that lead guard.

quotes.social_post: Brayden Burries says his current focus for growth is being more vocal on the floor, adding that he needs to be that lead guard for the team.

structured.context: Brayden Burries discusses his personal development as a playmaker and his goal to become a more vocal leader on the court.
